CONFIRMED 2026-09-10 by an independent filing, not merely inferred: Ohio BMV's own IRP Vehicle Status report for ZONE-OH's account (data/raw/permits/irp_status/, ingest/parse_irp_status.py) lists BOTH VINs as currently active, under the exact numbers '5852' and '5417' -- i.e. those are the STATE's own designations for these trucks, and '15852'/'5091' are the internal group unit workbook's alternate numbering for the identical VINs. owner_operator_self_pay._note: General policy, not a per-unit list: any of the 48 registered units flagged owner_operator=true in ingest/fleet_registry.py's registry() is the owner's own truck, and the owner-operator bears IRP and HVUT on it, not the operating company -- consistent with truck_breakeven.py and owner_operator.py already excluding an OO's own equipment costs from the company's side of the ledger. As of 2026-09-10 this resolves to units 5091 ($1,350.19, ZONE-operated -- operator says more detail is coming 'tomorrow', left as-is under this rule until then) and 8671 ($2,606.53, XTRACK-operated -- confirmed by the operator explicitly, 'he will be responsible for hvut and irp charges and we will deduct it from him' -- also one of the six lease-to-purchase VINs below, so the OO rule takes precedence over the lease-to-purchase one for this truck specifically). 7584 was ALSO an owner-operator truck but has its own bucket, departed_owner_operators, below -- that driver quit long ago and is excluded entirely rather than counted as a currently self-paying OO.

stated_driver_rate._note: Operator, 2026-09-10: 'those driver will be responsible for hvut cost which is 550$ each and irp amount that is 1880$ each unit' -- a STATED flat rate to charge these drivers, not each truck's own actual registration cost. CLAUDE.md already documents that IRP is apportioned per truck on miles and weight and runs $438-$1,430 a truck (3.3x spread) -- a flat $1,880 IRP rate is ABOVE that entire measured range, so this deducts MORE from most of these five drivers than the company actually paid the state for their trucks. Used here as the deduction amount because it is what will actually be charged/recovered, per the operator; the actual per-truck cost is kept alongside it (ltp_rate_comparison in attribute_by_responsibility()'s output) so the gap is visible, not hidden.

remaining_pool_split._note: Operator, 2026-09-10: 'rest units we spend money for irp and hvut should be equally divided between companies all units' -- every registered truck not covered by an owner-operator, investor, or lease-to-purchase-owner rule above is split EQUALLY across ZONE, XTRACK and AFG (1/3 each), replacing attribute()'s 'whichever company's P&L last carried it' rule for this specific cost. The two are different questions answered from the same data -- attribute() still shows who ran the truck; this shows who now pays for it -- and this file does not delete or override attribute(), it sits beside it.
